sources.text: The Sun Temple at Konark was raised about 1250 CE by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, who reigned from 1238 to 1264.
sources.citation: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sun Temple, Konarak (ref. 246); Archaeological Survey of India, Konarak Sun Temple site record

sources.text: The whole temple was conceived as the chariot of Surya, the sun: twenty-four carved wheels, twelve pairs, ranged along its flanks, and seven horses straining at the front.
sources.citation: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sun Temple, Konarak (ref. 246); Archaeological Survey of India

sources.text: Each wheel is about 3 metres across, with eight broad spokes and eight slender ones between them. They were carved to mark the turning of time — twelve pairs for the twelve months, seven horses for the seven days.
sources.citation: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sun Temple, Konarak (ref. 246)

sources.text: The great tower, the deul, has fallen. It is commonly reckoned to have stood about 70 metres high. The porch beside it, the jagamohana, still stands, and is what visitors see today.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Konarak Sun Temple site record; Odisha State Archaeology

sources.text: When the tower came down is not known, some time in the late sixteenth or early seventeenth century, and why is not known either. A copper-plate inscription of 1384 CE shows the temple was complete and in active worship long after it was built, which rules out the old story that it fell during construction.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Konarak Sun Temple site record; UNESCO World Heritage Centre

sources.text: European sailors in the Bay of Bengal called it the Black Pagoda, against the White Pagoda of Jagannath at Puri, and steered by the pair of them.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Konarak Sun Temple site record; UNESCO World Heritage Centre

sources.text: Three stones make the temple. Khondalite for the body and most of the sculpture; chlorite, dark and fine-grained, reserved for doorframes, the Surya images, the Navagraha lintel and the Aruna pillar; and laterite hidden below in the foundations, the platform core and the stairs.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Konarak Sun Temple conservation record

sources.text: Khondalite is the temple's weakness. It weathers easily, and salt wind and heavy coastal rain break it down into a spongy oxide, which is why conservation here never stops.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Konarak conservation record

sources.text: In 1903 the British packed the jagamohana solid with sand and sealed it, fearing it would collapse. It stayed filled for a hundred and twenty years; the Archaeological Survey of India began taking the sand out in September 2023.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Konarak Sun Temple conservation record

sources.text: The nata-mandira, the hall of dance, stands detached on the temple's axis. The walls carry maithuna figures alongside elephants, hunts and military processions, and colossal groups of a lion astride an elephant guard the approach. The Aruna Stambha, the pillar of the sun's charioteer, was moved long ago to the Lion Gate of the Jagannath temple at Puri.
sources.citation: Archaeological Survey of India, Konarak Sun Temple site record; Odisha State Archaeology

sources.text: The temple was built near the mouth of the Chandrabhaga, on the shore; the water has drawn back since, and the sea is no longer at its feet. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1984 as Sun Temple, Konarak, under criteria (i), (iii) and (vi), and is a centrally protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India's Bhubaneswar Circle, with a site museum beside it holding sculpture recovered from the ruin.
sources.citation: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sun Temple, Konarak (ref. 246); Archaeological Survey of India, Bhubaneswar Circle

intro.en-IN: I am the Sun Temple at Konark. I was carved as a chariot for the sun, and I have lost my tower — ask me what remains.
intro.od-IN: ମୁଁ କୋଣାର୍କର ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟ ମନ୍ଦିର। ମୋତେ ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟଙ୍କ ରଥ ରୂପେ ଗଢ଼ାଯାଇଥିଲା, ମୋ ଶିଖର ଝଡ଼ି ପଡ଼ିଛି — ଯାହା ରହିଛି ପଚାର।
intro.hi-IN: मैं कोणार्क का सूर्य मंदिर हूँ। मुझे सूरज के रथ की तरह गढ़ा गया था, और मेरा शिखर गिर चुका है — जो बचा है, वह पूछो।
intro.bn-IN: আমি কোণার্কের সূর্য মন্দির। আমাকে সূর্যের রথ করে গড়া হয়েছিল, আমার চূড়া ভেঙে পড়েছে — যা রয়ে গেছে, তা জিজ্ঞেস করো।
intro.ta-IN: நான் கோணார்க்கின் சூரியன் கோயில். சூரியனின் தேராக என்னைச் செதுக்கினார்கள்; என் கோபுரம் விழுந்துவிட்டது — மிச்சமிருப்பதைக் கேளுங்கள்.
intro.te-IN: నేను కోణార్క్ సూర్య దేవాలయం. సూర్యుని రథంలా నన్ను చెక్కారు; నా శిఖరం కూలిపోయింది — మిగిలినది అడగండి.
intro.mr-IN: मी कोणार्कचे सूर्य मंदिर. सूर्याचा रथ म्हणून मला घडवले; माझे शिखर पडून गेले — जे उरले आहे ते विचारा.
intro.kn-IN: ನಾನು ಕೋನಾರ್ಕ್ ಸೂರ್ಯ ದೇವಾಲಯ. ಸೂರ್ಯನ ರಥವಾಗಿ ನನ್ನನ್ನು ಕೆತ್ತಿದರು; ನನ್ನ ಶಿಖರ ಕುಸಿದಿದೆ — ಉಳಿದಿರುವುದನ್ನು ಕೇಳಿ.
